investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 22:35 and 22:42 UTC on 2026-07-21 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new agent pods. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated; the other 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler could not preempt any existing workload to free capacity. As a result, every attempt to create a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~127–145 s), and the eval probe never reached the point where it could write orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent workloads or other peer-pod consumers have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's affinity rules may have become overly restrictive, reducing the schedulable node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster was sized with only 2 kata-capable nodes, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations (runner uses withCleanup at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883, but prior failed runs may not have completed cleanup).

Verify that the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs correctly releases kata.peerpods.io/vm resources even when the probe fails mid-execution, to prevent future slot leaks.

Once capacity is restored, re-run all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm they pass and produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (allocatable > used) on the 2 kata nodes at the time of the failure would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis.

A passing run of remote-agent-create immediately after the failure window, with vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], would indicate the failure was transient and not a sustained capacity problem.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no longer exists on any node) and that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were actually free would shift the root cause to affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
Logs showing the remote-agent API returned an error before the Kubernetes scheduler was even invoked would indicate the failure originated upstream of the cluster scheduler.
A passing result on remote-agent-create while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime still fail would disprove the shared-dependency hypothesis and suggest check-specific issues.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.
Add an eval that detects and alerts on leaked remote-agent pods (Pending > N seconds or Running without an active eval session) to catch withCleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least one schedulable node exists for each required extended resource (kata.peerpods.io/vm) before remote-agent evals run.

Consider adding a latency regression eval that alerts when remote-agent pod scheduling time exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) as an early warning before the full 127s+ unschedulable timeout is reached.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-21T22:37–22:42Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the cluster's 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response payload, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod timed out unscheduled (~127–145 s per attempt). This is a cluster-level infrastructure constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production incident or real-traffic impact is present in the packet; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the inability to provision eval-time agent pods.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 145s.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable condition, pod stuck 142s, endedAt 2026-07-21T22:40:07.232Z.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the agent runtime was never reached.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — the agent creation step is the first blocking call, and it depends on a schedulable pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the check failed well within that window (150958ms), confirming the failure is scheduling-driven, not a latency threshold breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods (from prior eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods) are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods nodes satisfy, so horizontal scaling to other nodes is not possible without matching node configuration.

Tertiary — pod cleanup failure from a prior eval run: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not successfully terminate a previous eval's agent pod, leaked pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if concurrent eval runs or user workloads increased demand, the fixed capacity of 2 nodes may be structurally insufficient for the current load.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > 0, allocated = 0) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling failure would have a different cause (e.g., a pod spec error or API admission rejection).

If the scheduler message were absent and the pod reached Running state but the agent runtime returned an empty or malformed response, the root cause would shift to an application-layer defect rather than a scheduling constraint.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime probe logic rather than shared pod scheduling infrastructure.

If a subsequent eval run with no concurrent workloads succeeded (pod scheduled, all 5 evidence fields present), that would confirm the failure is load/capacity-driven rather than a permanent configuration defect.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec were found to be misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no node carries), the root cause would be a pod spec misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.

Add a pod-leak detection eval that lists running remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-affinity validation eval that confirms at least one node satisfies the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, providing an early warning before the full agent lifecycle eval runs.

Consider a synthetic scheduling dry-run eval (kubectl --dry-run=server apply on the remote-agent pod spec) that validates schedulability without consuming VM slots, enabling faster detection of scheduling constraint failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 22:35 and 22:42 UTC on 2026-07-21 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new agent pods. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated; the other 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler could not preempt any existing workload to free capacity. As a result, every attempt to create a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~127–145 s), and the eval probe never reached the point where it could write orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 145s, endedAt 2026-07-21T22:42:38.190Z

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the VM was never allocated
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent workloads or other peer-pod consumers have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's affinity rules may have become overly restrictive, reducing the schedulable node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster was sized with only 2 kata-capable nodes, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations (runner uses withCleanup at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883, but prior failed runs may not have completed cleanup).

Identify and terminate any leaked or zombie remote-agent pods (Pending or Running) that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs, to free VM slots.

Determine whether the cluster's 2 kata-capable nodes provide sufficient VM slot capacity for concurrent production workloads plus eval probes; if not, provision additional kata-capable nodes or increase VM slot limits.
Review the pod's node affinity/selector rules to confirm the 4 non-kata nodes are intentionally excluded and that no label drift has occurred that would further restrict scheduling.
Verify that the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs correctly releases kata.peerpods.io/vm resources even when the probe fails mid-execution, to prevent future slot leaks.

Once capacity is restored, re-run all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm they pass and produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (allocatable > used) on the 2 kata nodes at the time of the failure would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis.

A passing run of remote-agent-create immediately after the failure window, with vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], would indicate the failure was transient and not a sustained capacity problem.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no longer exists on any node) and that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were actually free would shift the root cause to affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
Logs showing the remote-agent API returned an error before the Kubernetes scheduler was even invoked would indicate the failure originated upstream of the cluster scheduler.
A passing result on remote-agent-create while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime still fail would disprove the shared-dependency hypothesis and suggest check-specific issues.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.
Add an eval that detects and alerts on leaked remote-agent pods (Pending > N seconds or Running without an active eval session) to catch withCleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least one schedulable node exists for each required extended resource (kata.peerpods.io/vm) before remote-agent evals run.

Consider adding a latency regression eval that alerts when remote-agent pod scheduling time exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) as an early warning before the full 127s+ unschedulable timeout is reached.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-21T22:37–22:42Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the cluster's 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response payload, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod timed out unscheduled (~127–145 s per attempt). This is a cluster-level infrastructure constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production incident or real-traffic impact is present in the packet; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the inability to provision eval-time agent pods.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the check failed well within that window (150958ms), confirming the failure is scheduling-driven, not a latency threshold breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods (from prior eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods) are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods nodes satisfy, so horizontal scaling to other nodes is not possible without matching node configuration.

Tertiary — pod cleanup failure from a prior eval run: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not successfully terminate a previous eval's agent pod, leaked pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if concurrent eval runs or user workloads increased demand, the fixed capacity of 2 nodes may be structurally insufficient for the current load.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > 0, allocated = 0) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling failure would have a different cause (e.g., a pod spec error or API admission rejection).

If the scheduler message were absent and the pod reached Running state but the agent runtime returned an empty or malformed response, the root cause would shift to an application-layer defect rather than a scheduling constraint.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime probe logic rather than shared pod scheduling infrastructure.

If a subsequent eval run with no concurrent workloads succeeded (pod scheduled, all 5 evidence fields present), that would confirm the failure is load/capacity-driven rather than a permanent configuration defect.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec were found to be misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no node carries), the root cause would be a pod spec misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity (allocatable vs. allocated) before attempting remote-agent pod creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout failure.
Add a pod-leak detection eval that lists running remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-affinity validation eval that confirms at least one node satisfies the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, providing an early warning before the full agent lifecycle eval runs.

Consider a synthetic scheduling dry-run eval (kubectl --dry-run=server apply on the remote-agent pod spec) that validates schedulability without consuming VM slots, enabling faster detection of scheduling constraint failures.
